txt: A grunt of acknowledgement. "I *do* try to keep up with my own sources. Independent stuff. You can't believe half of what you hear out there..."
For a moment the lorryman is silent. Then he spits on the pavement. "Yeah, him."
He eyes you warily, unsure how to respond. This goes on for about two seconds, then...
He grinds a cigarette butt into the pavement and quickly lights another.

He laughs. Nervously. "No, it's, uh -- you know, the Samaran guy who likes to pretend he's some kinda businessman? He's just selling his employer's stuff. Stuff he *stole* after he broke the seals on his Humanox lorry."
He laughs. Nervously. "Sure I'm sure," he says. "His tribe are natural liars. It's in their blood..."
He relaxes, slightly. "People think it's so easy, being a lorry driver. Well it *isn't*, okay?"
He shakes his head sadly. "Trust me, brother, I've done the research. Fascist magic just ain't true."
He shakes his head. "My friend, I don't know what you're after, but I have to tell you there's no turning back time..."
He smirks. "I don't know what you're talking about."
He stares at the Yellow Man mug, then suddenly... he explodes: "HAHAHA! HAHAHA! Oh man! Oh... man, that's great. Look at that guy go. Haven't seen anything that funny in a while."
He takes a drag of his cigarette. "I've done the reading, I know what the *real* experts say. Our greatest days are behind us, and we're not going back."
He takes a long suck on his cigarette, appearing to savour the taste. "Since he left I haven't had anyone to talk to..."
His eyes dart between you and the lieutenant. "I'm not scared of you -- or the mob. I'm under the protection of the Lorrymen and Carters Guild."
On the bottom of the man's boots you see an intricate tangle of treads with no immediately discernible pattern.
Silence. The air between them becomes tense.
The lorry driver glares at you intently, then shrugs. "Then I guess they grow apples somewhere else. You can never really tell with those Kojkos. They're *everywhere* -- except their own homes."
The lorryman ignores the lieutenant. "My friend, I don't know what you're after, but I have to tell you there's no turning back time..."
The lorryman looks at you like he can't decide whether he wants to smash something or break down in tears. The silence is heavy and uncomfortable.
The lorryman raises an eyebrow. "This some kind of homo thing?"
The man bites his lip and drops the near-finished cigarette lingering between his fingers. He reaches for a new one.
The man drops the near-finished cigarette lingering between his fingers. He reaches for a new one, with a confident look.
The man pulls on his cigarette furiously, probably still thinking about mesquitos and ass cancer.
The man shakes his head, dismayed -- furiously pulling on his cigarette: "It's a fuckin' travesty, is what it is."
You can just make out a familiar pattern in the intricate tangle of treads on the rubber of his soles. It is the map of your city!
"'Cause that's what they're all called. Kojko Pitjic, Lzloslaw Kojko. Kojkowicz Someone. Low self-esteem those guys have. Mind you, they look Occidental, but they're not... *really* like us."
"'Cause there's no point, you hear me? Unless you believe in ancient fascist magic like some wannabe magus."
"'Cause you're a runt and an asshole."
"A lorry driver. Who drives a lorry. Or is sometimes stuck in traffic jams, guarding that lorry."
"Aces! Good to know the law's got our backs." He gives a quick two-finger salute. "For Revachol, the Suzerain! The world is our Suzerainty."
"Apples." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the stub across the street.
"Apples."
"Are you lost? You look lost. Out of place."
"Are you mocking me right now, runt?"
"As arbitrary as any judgement. That doesn't make it less of a fact. We all have to use *facts*. Once you accept it, you'll gain the clarity of understanding."
"Been admiring the stompers, eh?" He grins. "Sure thing, check 'em out." He lifts his left foot, then the right.
"C'mon, man, I just said 'Welcome to Revachol'... It's a lorry driver thing."
"C'mon, man, the holler... It's just a greeting. A lorry driver thing."
"Can't have it."
"Custom-made. Cost me a pretty penny!" He rubs the back of his balding head.
"Did you miss the part where I said they aren't here yet? Besides, even if I did have some I wouldn't go putting my nose in them..." He looks at you with a strange glint in his eyes.
"Don't make yourself too comfortable!"
"Don't push your luck, runt." The man gives you a disgusted look, then turns his attention elsewhere, ignoring your presence.
"Drugs? They're shit, man. I don't let anything pollute my body." He takes a long drag on his cigarette.
"Evidence of what? I haven't done anything." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Fine." He shrugs.
"For when the Invasion comes..." He glances at the lieutenant. "The last thing they'll see before the lights go out is *illustrious Revachol*."
"Fuck you, I told you. I'm not gonna..."
"Fucking... homo cop." A globule of sweat gathers at his brow.
"Go right ahead." The man scratches his heavyset stomach. "You may be a cop, but that won't help you avoid the calamity to come."
"God damn right. They've been trying to fuck us out of our heritage in the name of profits. But when they try to replace us they'll regret it."
"God damn..." He wipes the tears from his eyes. "Thanks for that. But no, it's not mine."

"Good. If we, the Evening People, pull together -- we can form a bulwark against these troubled times!" The man grins at you. "Root out the forces that seek to undermine the well-being of our people."
"Guess so." He grins, contented with himself.
"Ha ha! Welcome to Revachol!"
"He did *something* -- he stole his employer's goods and another, honest lorryman's job. You know..." His smirk turns into a suspicious grin.
"He did *something*. He stole his employer's goods and another, honest lorryman's job. Talk to him -- I don't know anything."
"He's the Samaran guy who likes to pretend he's some kinda businessman... Really he's just selling his employer's stuff. Stuff he *stole* after he broke the seals on his Humanox lorry."
"He's your man, alright. One-hundred percent. He's a lorryman selling his employer's stuff -- broke the seals on his Humanox lorry. No doubt he's selling drugs too."
"Heh." A condescending chortle. "I knew you people don't understand *poetry*."

"Hell no. It's a *guild*. Invitation only. Unions work for the rich fucks. They're basically the same. Been trying to fuck us out of our heritage in the name of profits. But you can't replace experience."
"Hello, compatriot!" He recognizes you. "You have something to discuss?"
"Hey man, you know. There are all sorts of Invasions... " He looks at his boots, then you. "I thought we could rely on the cops. We're in this together, whether you realize it or not."
"Hey, fuck you, alright? *We're* supposed to be the ones on top, not... you know..." He nods toward the gates.
"Hey, if the name and description fit by the very grace of nature, who am I to say otherwise?"
"His tribe are natural liars. It's in their blood..." He nods in a sagely manner, then another puff of that cigarette: "He's your man, alright. One-hundred percent."
"How about you fuck off? I ain't saying *anything*."
"I ain't saying nothing."
"I bet." His cool gaze pierces deep, with noxious effluence wafting in the surrounding air.
"I don't go for that foreign piss. Proper booze is made in Mundi, or sometimes I like a dram of that Yugo-Graad vodka. Kojko's ain't worth much, but they do know booze."
"I don't know shit, and if I did I wouldn't tell you." He puffs on his cigarette.
"I don't know, I don't even know her name. She just rolls with the fleet and acts like a big shot. Some dyke probably. I haven't even seen her for days."
"I don't think you're as *down* with our fight as you'd like me to believe, *brother*. Why's the saffron-man still there? Talk to him -- I don't know anything."
"I haven't learned anything I didn't know before." The lorryman shakes his head with indignation.
"I salute you, compatriot. Defenders of the Evening Lands have to stick together." He takes out a pack rolled up inside his sleeve. "Light up, brother. Ward off those jungle spirits."
"I'll believe it when I see it." He shrugs off your hand. "Whatever, I don't care. It's all the same to me..."
"I'm *not* in trouble right now -- and I don't have to tell you a single thing. Now fuck off."
"I'm here to pick up a load of fuckin' apples, man. Just regular, Kojko-picked apples."
"I'm not *just* racist. Look, I've read *books*," he gestures with his cigarette for emphasis. "The science of racial theory has all been proved, even if some people don't want to accept it."
"I'm not the only one. Look, I've read *books*," he gestures with his cigarette for emphasis. "The science of racial theory has all been proved, even if some people don't want to accept it."
"I've seen the demographic reports, I know what our experts say. Our greatest days as a people are behind us, and we're not going back."
"I've told you everything I've got." He looks around nervously. "Can you please stop talking to me now?"
"If you don't know, I ain't telling you shit."
"Isn't it obvious? Fuckin' Siileng, that beady-eyed South-Samaran." He spits on the ground. "His little side business is a scam. I wouldn't be surprised if he was peddling drugs as well."
"It sure is!"
"It's Revachol!"
"It's about preserving our heritage, our *birthright*."
"It's about... biological determinism. Natural law. The sorting of the races." He spits on the ground.
"It's my last one."

"It's true." He pushes on. "Also, you need to realize the dangers of *mixing races*. Who knows what might happen if people don't stay in their birthplace? You might end up with a new sub-race, with unknown characteristics, leading to extra competition. That's why you've got to *control* the offspring."

"It's what the kipts of Boogie Street are going for -- right under our noses. And the others too, on the radio. Heard any *chansons* lately? Heard any *mottettos* or *lieder*? No. Dominating culture is how they plan to win. They say so themselves."
"Just follow the smell. It smells like apricots and *oil* when you're nearby..." The lorryman lets out a raspy croak at his own sense of humour.
"Just the truth." The man shrugs. "I'm a truth-teller, above all else."
"Let's get one thing straight: You can't tell a man to 'fuck off' and then say he's your brother. It doesn't work like that..."
"Like fuck you are. Why's your partner a multi-ethnic rainbow man? Why'd you not arrest Siileng? Fuck off, I ain't telling you shit."
"Listen up, fuckwit. You don't scare me. You cops don't run Revachol West. You don't run Martinaise. You don't run shit."
"Look, I'm gonna be straight with you since you're my kin. I don't know shit. And if I did I wouldn't tell you. You're a cop, I'm not an idiot." He puffs on his cigarette.
"Look, ace detective, I come from a long line of lorrymen. We got ancient rights and privileges..." He loses his patience for explaining it.
"Look, fuck you, man!" He tries to wave you off. "It's some lorry down there, green banged up thing. I don't fucking *know* who she is."
"Looking for something, runt? Come to tell me to fuck off again?"
"Looking for something?" The lorry driver recognizes you.
"Make me, runt." He blows a cloud of smoke right in front of your face.
"Mhmhm, I see..." The lorryman takes a long drag from his cigarette.
"My... what? Ah!" He jumps back with a look of disgust. "Fucking puffs everywhere..."
"Nah. You wouldn't just leave him out there if you..." He tries to light a fresh cigarette, but his hands are shaking now. The sentence simply ends.
"No I'm not. I'm not coming anywhere -- and you're not taking me there. Now fuck off."
"No, I can't help you." He clears his throat. "And I'll tell you why..."
"No, that's bullshit. We can't turn back time, but that doesn't mean we can just surrender to the savages..."
"No. It's not like that." He looks at his shoes. "You don't get it, it's... when I kick them you know? Fuck it. It's too complex for you."
"No."
"Not at all! We're part of a guild and everything... it's very ancient, very prestigious."
"Not in, not out. I'll never betray the purity of my tribe."
"Not much anymore. I'm here to pick up some cargo, but the dockworkers are on strike, so... it's a sit-and-wait-on-your-ass situation."
"Not the most popular topic nowadays, with the Coalition in charge and all. You might want to *change the topic* -- that is, bury your head under the sand like common sheep."
"Now what makes you think I know how to 'turn back time'?"
"Of course he's a lorry driver! What -- he tell you he's just some simple businessman or some shit? He's selling his employer's stuff after he broke the seals on his Humanox lorry."
"Oh yeah?" he snarls. "And what goods are those?"
"Oh, *that* old song." He spits.
"Oh, I'm just a simple camionneur, a father of three, and a Revachol patriot."
"Oh, yeah?" He looks intrigued.
"Oh?" The man seems mildly disappointed that you don't want to hear more of his lecture.

"Open your eyes. Haven't you noticed something different lately? An unfortunate downturn, maybe? When members of the superior race cease to believe in their innate superiority, they stop competing for resources."
"Oughtta what, officer?" The man looks at you coolly, noxious effluence wafting in the air around him.
"Our race does, man. That's the whole idea. If we don't get 'em, the kipts and the Kojkos will. It's just biological reality."
"Past the monument, down there," he waves south. "The green 'Tempo'. Now leave me the fuck alone, okay?"
"People today, they only look at what's on the surface. These women, they all want a guy who looks like Kipty the Kipt over there." He nods to the gate.
"People who've studied these things say that we are superior by design. So, naturally, we Occidentals should be in charge. Obviously you can see the merits in that."
"Saffron picker! Welcome to Revachol!"
"Seriously, though, he's usually just a little bit south of here. Down near the canal, you can't miss him. Just watch yourself..."
"So you heading off or what?" He clears his throat, doing his best to appear indifferent.
"So, lately we Occidentals have experienced an unfortunate downturn: when members of the superior race cease to believe in their innate superiority, they stop competing for resources."
"Someone with a cart, what did you think it was? That's how deep into history our thing reaches -- before machines."
"Sorry I couldn't be of any help." He gives you an ambivalently mocking half-nod.
"Sorry, all done." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Suit yourself, officer. Hide your face in the sand if you so wish." He spits on the ground.
"Sure fucking is! We have a guild and everything... very ancient, very prestigious."
"That's the one, brother. His tribe are natural liars. It's in their blood." The lorryman looks at you with appreciation and understanding.
"That's the one. His tribe are natural liars. It's in their blood..." The lorryman takes a slow, satisfied drag and blows a smoke ring.
"That's the question, isn't it?" He takes a drag. "People think you and me got it so easy. But the reality is it's fucking *hard* to be a regular guy these days..."
"That's too bad. It's all done for." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.

"The problem? The damn kipts are showing a real good game lately! Same with the mesquitos. And all the other intruder species out there, breeding like rabbits. They're on the precipice of cultural victory."
"The stench is getting unbearable." He turns to you. "Is there a reason you're bothering me?"
"The strike? They've been at it for a while. A month, two months maybe?" He gestures towards the lorries. "But *this* here is just the last week or so."
"They don't *care* if you're a good guy. They're superficial creatures. That's just the truth." He takes a long drag.
"They know they can't beat us in a fair fight, so they have to get us to weaken ourselves somehow. It's racial sabotage. Racial *economic* sabotage."

"This concerns you, policeman, so you better be *vigilant*. The kipts are showing a good game lately, same with the mesquitos. And the other intruder species out there, breeding like rabbits. They're on the precipice of cultural victory."

"Time, yeah... Listen, man, do you even understand how *hard* we've got it? How completely *stacked* the whole rotten deck is against people like you and me?" He takes a furious drag of his cigarette.
"Trusting street thugs with their goods is going to fuck 'em right up the ass, mark my words. Generations of practice ain't no laughing matter."
"Uh..." Your sudden change of heart catches him off guard. "I uh... well... yeah fuck it, it's a stupid question anyway."
"Welcome to Re..." The fat man stops mid-sentence as he notices Lieutenant Kitsuragi.
"Welcome to Revachol! Don't stay too long."
"Welcome to Revachol!" The lorry driver recognizes you. "Got rid of the other one, eh? Good call."
"Welcome to Revachol!" announces the rotund man. The remark isn't addressed to you. It’s addressed to the lieutenant.
"Welcome to Revachol!" the rotund man announces. He has a lit cigarette between his fingers.
"Welcome to Revachol!"
"What do you mean by 'big time' racist, exactly?" He stares at you intently.

"What do you think? I can't leave the lorry unguarded. Stuff's been getting looted lately. It's those little kipts sneaking around at night... If they touch my stuff, the bosses will be on my ass like ass cancer."
"What is there to talk about? It's a racist world. I didn't make it that way. And neither did you -- and *you're* a racist too!"
"What is there to talk about? It's a racist world. I didn't make it that way. I'm just living in it -- surviving in it. That's all this is. Survival."
"What's a guy like *me* supposed to do, huh? Fucking butt-clenches while I'm driving, like some kind of anal acrobat in the homo circus?!"
"What, aren't we *allowed* to say that it's the kipts who do all the stealing around here? It's not *rotor science*, man..."
"What? Here on the street? You won't." He shakes his head. "Now fuck off."
"What? I don't wanna hear about your bum-play! I'm trying to tell you what life is like out there for the working man and you're going on about sphincters."
"What?" The lorryman erupts in contemptuous laughter. "What do you think we're doing right now, runt? We're outside, talking!"
"What?"
"Whatever you say, *officers*." He waits impassively, cigarette smouldering between his fingers.
"Whatever, go back to your college class, bino."
"When the next wave of the Invasion comes -- the last thing they'll see before the lights go out is *illustrious Revachol*."
"Why would I do that? I am an honest man." He puts out his cigarette and flicks the tiny stub toward the street.
"Ye... no... never mind, officer. Pleased to meet you. I'm a camionneur, a father of three, and a Revacholian patriot."
"Yeah, I drive a lorry. Back and forth. Sometimes I sit stuck in a traffic jam, guarding that lorry."

"Yeah, I knew that guy. He was an honest driver who loved his country. We were having a good debate about genetics at the Whirling-in-Rags when some kipt-boys smashed his lock and took damn near everything. Lost his fucking job over it."
"Yeah, apples... I take it you had other questions?"
"Yeah, they're a big deal. My great-grandfather was a carter. Had a royal license and everything. We've tried to hold on to our privileges."
"Yeah," he hisses, "sounds about right."
"Yeah," he says, unsure where this is leading. "They're his little bitches. He's got them all over the unions."
"Yeah? Says who?"
"Yes, sir." He gives you a tiny mock salute. "Pleased to meet you, officer. I'm a camionneur, a father of three, and a Revacholian patriot."
"You know where that shit comes from? Saramiriza, Safre, Iilmaraa. They take the money from our local junkies here and then use it to out-compete us in the manufacturing sector."
"You know, I get funny looks from people all the time. I *know* they're looking at my gut. I can *see* that. Big fucking deal, a guy put on a little weight, who cares?"
"You know: Graadniks. Graadvolk. The degenerates from Graad."
"You still with us, runt? Or are you just gonna stand around like a glue-sniffer?"
"You think it's *easy* to stay in shape driving a lorry six days a week?!" His voice is unnaturally shrill. "You guys got it easy, on your feet all day long, burning calories and what not..."
"You two make a cute couple, you know that?" The lorryman spits.
"You'll see when the time comes, officer," he grins and caresses the side of his boot. "*True* patriots carry Revachol in their very soles."
"You're all bark and no bite. The real dogs are up in Jamrock. Everyone knows that."
"You're not peones," he says. "You wouldn't be investigating a drug-thing, if you were."
"Your 'gut', huh?" He stares at you intently.
"Yup, it's one of their main exports. They grow 'em down south Yekokataa. A beautiful place, got great scenic vistas."
